answers.answer: A player rules a clearing by having more total warriors plus buildings there than each other player. Tokens and pawns do not count. An ordinary tie means nobody rules; the Eyrie wins a tie for most if it has at least one Eyrie piece there. The Vagabond cannot rule or prevent another player from ruling.
answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle, Rule (2.5): ‘warriors plus buildings’; tokens and pawns excluded; ordinary ties and Eyrie tie exception stated.

answers.answer: A normal move takes any positive number of the mover’s warriors or pawns along a linking path from one clearing to an adjacent clearing, and the mover must rule the origin, destination, or both. Rule is rechecked for each move. The same pieces may move repeatedly, including in multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly says otherwise.
answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, ‘Move (4.2)’ states positive group, path, rule condition, repeated moves, and river restriction.

answers.answer: The defender may play one matching-suit Ambush (birds are wild). The attacker may foil it with a matching Ambush; the defender’s card is discarded and a foiled Ambush deals no hits. Otherwise the defender immediately deals two hits and discards the card. If no attacking warriors or Vagabond pawn remain, battle ends immediately. Resolve before-roll effects, roll, after-roll effects, count hits, then deal hits. Higher die is the attacker’s rolled hits and lower die the defender’s (equal dice give equal results); each side’s rolled hits are capped by its own warriors in battle. Alliance defense reverses the dice; the Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead of warriors. Add extra hits without a warrior cap and subtract ignored hits; an attacker gets one defenseless hit if the defender has no warriors, or if the defender is the Vagabond and has no undamaged swords. Each hit removes an opposing piece. The side taking hits chooses its removal order, but must remove all its warriors before buildings or tokens. Both sides deal their counted hits even if warriors are removed during that step. Whoever removes an enemy building or token scores one VP each, even when defending or outside battle. Vagabond hits damage items.
answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle, ‘Battle (4.3)’ steps 1–6.

answers.answer: Crafting uses crafting icons at the bottom left of a card, activating matching crafting pieces rather than paying the card’s suit. A crafting piece can activate only once per turn, except the Vagabond may reactivate its pawn by exhausting more hammers. An item card cannot be crafted if that item is absent from the map supply. You cannot craft a persistent effect identical to one already in your play area.
answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, ‘Craft (4.1)’ and its immediate-effect and persistent-effect bullets.

answers.answer: During your own Daylight, at 10 or more VP, you may activate a dominance card from your hand, put it in your play area, remove your score marker, and stop scoring VP. At the start of your own Birdsong, win by ruling three clearings of the matching mouse, rabbit, or fox suit; bird dominance requires ruling two diagonally opposite corner clearings. Meeting the condition earlier does not win immediately. An activated dominance card cannot be removed or replaced.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Dominance (3.3).

answers.answer: When a dominance card would be discarded, put it near the map as available instead. During your own Daylight, spend a matching-suit card to take an available dominance card into your hand. An available bird dominance card remains bird, so it must be paid for with a bird card; a bird card can pay for a non-bird dominance card. Taking a card and activating it are separate and do not use a faction action allowance.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Dominance (3.3), card availability and taking rules.

answers.answer: In Standard Setup with two players, remove all four dominance cards before shuffling the shared deck, then each player draws three cards. Cover the four R building slots with ruins. The map item supply is 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, and 2 coins. Keep the four R-marked bag, boot, hammer, and sword separate; only a Vagabond setup hides one under each ruin, and without a Vagabond the ruins contain no items. Set factions up in letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond; this is distinct from turn order.
answers.evidence: Setup → Standard Setup steps 3–7 and ‘Vagabond setup (9.3)’.

answers.answer: Only the Marquise may place pieces in the Keep’s clearing, though other players may move pieces into it. If any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, the Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of returning them to supply; this can apply outside battle. If the Keep is gone, there is no destination for Field Hospitals. The Keep cannot be placed again if removed.
answers.evidence: Actions → Marquise de Cat, ‘Keep’ and ‘Field Hospitals’.

answers.answer: Marquise Daylight begins with crafting using workshops, followed by up to three actions plus one action per bird card spent outside an action. Actions may be taken in any order and number, subject to Recruit’s once-per-turn limit. March is up to two moves; the moves may use the same or different warriors, and the compound March cannot be interrupted to spend a bird card or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter, once per turn; if supply is insufficient, place as many as possible, choosing among eligible recruiters. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill’s clearing to place one wood there.
answers.evidence: Actions → Marquise de Cat, Daylight and the Battle, March, Recruit, and Overwork bullets.

answers.answer: To build, choose a clearing you rule with an open building slot, choose the building type, and take the leftmost building of that type from its track. Pay the cost shown atop its column by removing that many wood from the target clearing or from other ruled clearings connected to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score the VP on the newly uncovered track space. The full wood cost, building piece, and legal slot are required.
answers.evidence: Actions → Marquise de Cat, Daylight ‘Build’ bullet.

answers.answer: Eyrie Birdsong: (1) if its hand is empty, draw one card for Emergency Orders; (2) add one or two hand cards to any Decree columns, with at most one added bird card; (3) if there are no roosts on the map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can be placed.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Birdsong steps 1–3.

answers.answer: In Daylight, craft with roosts first, then resolve every Decree card column by column in Recruit, Move, Battle, Build order. Within a column, card order is freely chosen; bird is wild. Recruit places a warrior at a roost in a clearing matching the card (two with Charismatic). Move must move at least one warrior from a matching clearing and meet ordinary move requirements. Battle must be initiated in a matching clearing with Eyrie warriors and an enemy. Build places a roost in a matching clearing the Eyrie rules, with an open slot and no roost already there. If any required action cannot be fully completed, including because of unavailable pieces, enter Turmoil immediately; do not skip that card or continue other columns.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Daylight, ‘resolve the Decree’ and its Recruit, Move, Battle, Build requirements.

answers.answer: In Turmoil, lose one VP per bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard every Decree card except Viziers; flip the current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement (if none are face up, flip all leaders face up first); retuck Viziers into the new leader’s columns. Daylight ends and the Eyrie proceeds to Evening. Map warriors and buildings are not removed. Evening scoring and drawing still occur after Turmoil.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → ‘Turmoil, in order’ and Evening.

answers.answer: Outrage triggers when another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. That player adds one matching hand card, with birds counting, to Supporters; moving a group costs one card per affected move, not per warrior. If they have no matching card including birds, they show their hand to the Alliance, which draws one card from the deck into Supporters. Supporters are capped at five when the Alliance has no bases; incoming cards over capacity are discarded. With any base, the stack is unlimited.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Guerrilla War / Supporters and ‘Outrage’ paragraphs.

answers.answer: Both actions are in Birdsong, with Revolt first and Spread Sympathy second; the Alliance may do any number of each. Revolt chooses a sympathetic clearing without a base that matches a base still on the Alliance board, spends two matching supporters, removes all enemy pieces there, places the matching base, places warriors equal to the number of sympathetic clearings matching that base’s printed suit, and adds one officer. Spread Sympathy chooses an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy (or any clearing if there is no sympathy), and spends the matching supporter cost shown above the next sympathy token. For Spread Sympathy only, Martial Law adds one matching supporter if one other player has at least three warriors in the chosen clearing. Revolt scores normal VP for removed enemy buildings/tokens; enemy Vagabond damages three items instead of being removed. Sympathy places a token and scores the uncovered track VP; only one sympathy per clearing, and the Keep’s placement ban applies. If Revolt placements cannot all be completed, place the maximum possible; no extra base-placement prerequisite is added.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Birdsong, Revolt and Spread Sympathy rules.

answers.answer: Train in Daylight by spending a hand card matching a clearing with an Alliance base to place one warrior from supply in the Officers box; Supporters cannot pay for Train. In Evening, take military operations up to the number of officers; officers remain on the board after use. When a base is removed, discard all Supporters matching its clearing, including birds, and remove half the officers rounded up. If no bases remain, discard excess Supporters down to five.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance → ‘Losing a base’, Daylight Train, and Evening military operations.

answers.answer: At Birdsong, refresh two exhausted items per tea already face up on the Refresh track, then three more; tea refreshed during this step gives no extra refresh that step. Slip is optional and moves to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors; it ignores effects that prevent movement out of a clearing. Vagabond Daylight Move exhausts one boot plus one extra boot if the destination has any warriors of a Hostile faction, including for forced moves; it ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest can move only to an adjacent clearing. In Evening, if in a forest, Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up; ready tea, coins, and bags move to their tracks if able. Rest does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. The Vagabond always draws one card plus one for each face-up coin on its track, even after Rest.
answers.evidence: Vagabond → Birdsong Refresh and Slip, Daylight Move, and Evening steps 1–2.

answers.answer: Explore exhausts a torch in a ruin’s clearing, takes one hidden item face up into Satchel or a matching track, and scores one VP if an item is taken; remove the ruin when its last item is taken, freeing the slot. For a Quest, choose a face-up quest matching the clearing and exhaust its two listed items; complete it and choose either VP equal to the number of matching completed quests including this one, or draw two cards. Reveal a replacement quest. Repair exhausts a hammer to move one damaged item to Satchel while keeping its current face; ready tea, coins, or bags move to their tracks if there is room.
answers.evidence: Vagabond → Daylight Explore, Quest, and Repair bullets.

answers.answer: Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes that faction Hostile, except for the special allied-warrior battle-loss rule. On the Vagabond’s own turn, in battle, Infamy gives one extra VP per hostile piece removed, except the warrior that first made that faction Hostile. There is no Infamy while defending on another player’s turn or from Strike. Aid cannot move a Hostile marker out of Hostile. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in the clearing; only if that enemy has no warriors there may it remove another piece of that faction instead. Strike is not battle and yields no Infamy.
answers.evidence: Vagabond → Relationships, Hostile / Infamy, and Strike bullets.

answers.answer: The Vagabond cannot activate normal dominance to win. With four or more players, during its own Daylight at 10 or more VP, it may activate dominance to form a coalition with a player not already in a coalition who has the lowest VP among the other players, choosing among ties. The Vagabond places its score marker on the partner’s faction board and stops scoring. If the partner wins, the Vagabond also wins, including when the partner wins by dominance. If the partner is Hostile, that relationship resets to Indifferent. Coalition partners are not enemies, and coalition alone grants no Allied relationship powers.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Vagabond coalition (9.2.8).
